selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What happens to a big joy when a person thinks only about this world?
questions.answer: It turns into deep sadness.

questions.question: What wrong idea does the second man have about those who left?
questions.answer: He thinks they are gone into misery and cut off completely.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the grave seem to be for believers?
questions.answer: It seems like a passage to where loved ones have gone.

questions.question: What three reactions are believers told to avoid toward death and the grave?
questions.answer: Fear, anxiety, and turning away.

questions.question: Why is that excuse not accepted?
questions.answer: Because the basic truths of death and human need still remain.

questions.question: Why is copying the crowd not a safe guide?
questions.answer: Because the crowd can only accompany a person to the grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the human journey through life?
questions.answer: It does not stop; it moves even faster.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: It is compared to a whirling dervish moving in order toward high goals.

questions.question: What future change will happen when the earth dislikes human wrongdoing?
questions.answer: It will erase those corrupt works from its face.

questions.question: How can hardship be linked to sins in the passage?
questions.answer: It can serve as payment for sins tied to not thanking Allah.

questions.question: What is the main warning at the start of the passage about loving only worldly life?
questions.answer: Focusing only on this life can make a person suffer badly.

questions.question: Why does the second man suffer more than the first?
questions.answer: Because he thinks separation means complete loss.

questions.question: Why does that comfort not solve his real problem?
questions.answer: Because his real pain comes from his wrong understanding of separation.

questions.question: What does the passage say to do instead of avoiding the subject of death?
questions.answer: Face it bravely and think about its meaning.

questions.question: What modern-sounding statement does the passage tell the nafs not to make?
questions.answer: That this age is different and everyone is absorbed in worldly living.

questions.question: What excuse about modern times does the passage reject?
questions.answer: The excuse that this age is different and everyone is too busy with worldly life.

questions.question: What does the eye of wisdom help a person notice in the world?
questions.answer: That everything is arranged with order and purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage say is wrong about claiming disaster victims’ losses are pointless?
questions.answer: It removes hope and treats their suffering unfairly.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest the earth may be rejecting?
questions.answer: Certain forms of human heedlessness and wrongdoing.

questions.question: What future cleansing of the earth is described?
questions.answer: The earth will remove ugly deeds that dishonor its surface.

questions.question: What big idea is taught through the example of the two men?
questions.answer: The way a person understands death and separation changes whether he feels hope or pain.

questions.question: How does the first man react to news of his own departure?
questions.answer: He welcomes it happily.

questions.question: What does the one remaining guest represent for the second man?
questions.answer: A weak attempt to replace many lost relationships.

questions.question: What attitude should replace fear of death?
questions.answer: Brave acceptance and trust.
